brief.story:
Anthropic announced on September 16, 2026, that it is collapsing its two main Claude work modes — Claude Chat (for quick questions) and Claude Cowork (for longer, multi-step agentic tasks) — into a single interface the company calls "one Claude." Starting that day, Claude Cowork and chat are merging into one Claude, so users can bring a quick question or hand over a report due at noon, and Claude takes it from there, even after they've closed their laptops.

Why the merger:
The official Anthropic blog post explains the rationale directly: "We built Cowork as a separate place for bigger work, and Design for visual work. People used both, and told us the frustrating part was deciding where a task belonged." Anthropic had previously separated large tasks into Cowork and visual production into Claude Design, but users had to judge the type of task before making a request, and content started in one couldn't easily carry over to the other.

What changes for users:
Anthropic unified Claude Chat and Claude Cowork into "one Claude" — rather than separating the space for quick questions from the space for multi-step work involving files and tools, Claude will now draw on whatever capabilities it needs from any conversation. Users no longer have to decide up front whether to open "the chat" or "the work mode." The company describes this as more a product change than a model change — this isn't a new AI, it's a simpler way to reach capabilities Anthropic already had spread across different surfaces.

As a result of the merger, Claude will drop from three to two modes: Claude Chat and Claude Code. Claude Code, the coding-focused product for terminal and IDE work, is not affected by this consolidation.

New tools — Claude Docs and Claude Slides:
Claude Docs and Claude Slides are new as of September 16, and Claude Design now works inside conversations too. Users can ask for a document and write it together with Claude, or ask for a presentation and Claude drafts the slides. Users can edit directly, present straight from Claude, or download as PowerPoint or PDF. All three are in beta on paid plans, and Enterprise admins choose when to turn them on.

Claude Docs exports to Word, PDF, Markdown, and Google Docs; Claude Slides can be presented in Claude or downloaded as PowerPoint or PDF. Docs supports viewer and editor roles, but has no version history or comment-only access.

Claude Design:
Claude Design is a collaborative visual creation tool released by Anthropic Labs on April 17, 2026, that lets users generate designs, prototypes, slides, and marketing materials through natural-language prompts. Claude Design is now available inside regular conversations while remaining usable as a standalone product.

Sharing and control:
Anthropic says anything made with Design, Slides, or Docs lives at one shareable link that opens on a phone, and users can leave a comment for Claude on a slide. Claude asks before acting by default, though an optional setting allows it to keep working and check in only when closer review is needed. Users retain final say.

Rollout plan:
Anthropic is rolling out "one Claude" on Pro and Max plans over the next few weeks, will extend it to Team and Free plans soon, and will expand it to Enterprise plans after notifying administrators at least 30 days ahead of the change. Cowork as a separate product is being folded into the main Claude interface; its agentic capabilities remain — only the separate entry point goes away.

For existing Cowork users:
The official blog post says everything is where users left it — chats, projects, artifacts, connectors, and skills — and when they open the app, they can pick up where they left off. There is nothing to turn on.

Background on Cowork:
The merger comes only eight months after Anthropic introduced Cowork as a research preview on January 12, 2026. At launch it was much narrower: Cowork initially appeared as a Claude Max feature in the macOS desktop application, bringing the agentic pattern of Claude Code to non-technical work. Anthropic's idea was essentially to take the agentic architecture behind Claude Code and expose it to people who did not live in a terminal.

The quote in the source:
Andrew Keller, identified as Senior Economist, is quoted in the official Anthropic blog post: "I could have Claude pull up [my legal research database], and it would pull all the cases, read them, figure out which other cases I might need, download them, and store them in a folder for my personal review."

What the sources don't answer:
- It is not confirmed which model(s) power the unified Claude experience.
- No firm timeline is given for when Team and Free plan users will receive the update.
- The full range of collaboration controls and template options for Docs and Slides are not detailed in the sources.
- Export of documents to Microsoft Word or Google Docs is reported only by SiliconANGLE and other secondary outlets, not confirmed directly in Anthropic's own blog post.

sourceTexts.title: Anthropic merges its chat and agentic products into one AI assistant in push to build a superapp | Fortune
sourceTexts.text:
Anthropic is merging its agentic tool—Claude Cowork—and its chatbot—Claude Chat—into a single product.The change, which takes effect Wednesday, is also happening alongside the introduction of two new beta products, Claude Docs and Claude Slides, alongside a wider rollout of Anthropic’s Claude Design tool, which will now be available inside every conversation rather than as a standalone product.

It’s part of a broader industry push to build an AI “everything app”—a single interface designed to replace a growing collection of separate tools for searching, writing, coding, managing files and carrying out routine work. The premise is that users should not have to decide which specialized AI product to open, or manually shuttle context between them: the assistant should retain the thread of a task and select the relevant tools itself. For AI companies, the approach also creates a more direct relationship with users, increases the time they spend inside one product and makes it easier to bundle premium capabilities into a subscription.

It’s also an attempt to court enterprise customers as businesses attempt to centralize and control their employees’ AI use. OpenAI has been pursuing a similar strategy and plans to fold ChatGPT, its Codex coding agent, and potentially its Atlas browser into a single “superapp” meant to cut down on fragmentation and let the AI move between researching, coding, and explaining within one session. Anthropic’s own coding-focused product, Claude Code, remains separate for now.

Anthropic frames the change as simplifying the user experience. Under the new setup, users no longer have to decide upfront whether a task should be given to Claude Chat or to Cowork, Anthropic’s more autonomous, task-execution product.

Slides can be drafted, edited and presented directly from Claude, or downloaded as PowerPoint or PDF files. Docs, the newest addition, lets multiple colleagues collaborate on a document in real time, with Claude drafting sections and commenting alongside human editors; exports to Google Docs and Microsoft Word are supported at launch.The company said the rollout starts with Pro and Max subscribers on web, desktop and mobile, with Team and Free plans to follow.

But the shift may also carry cost implications. Agentic products like Cowork, which reason through multi-step tasks and make tool calls on a user’s behalf, tend to consume more tokens than a simple chat exchange—and token usage is what AI companies bill on.

For example, a Stanford Digital Economy Lab study of coding tasks found that agentic tasks consumed roughly 1,000 times more tokens than simple chat reasoning tasks. If simple queries inside “one Claude” end up routed through more agentic, tool-calling machinery by default, that could push up the compute cost of answering even straightforward questions.

Anthropic said users will retain control over how autonomously Claude works. By default, Claude will ask before taking an action, though users can let it continue working and check in only when something needs closer review. Enterprise administrators, meanwhile, can decide when to enable the beta Docs, Slides, and Design features for their organizations.

sourceTexts.title: Anthropic Merges Claude Chat and Cowork Into One Window
sourceTexts.text:
Anthropic collapsed Claude’s separate chat, Cowork and Artifacts surfaces into a single window on September 16, 2026, and handed the job of picking the right tool to Claude itself. Pro and Max subscribers get the change first.

The Big Picture

Anthropic merged Claude’s chat, Cowork and Artifacts surfaces into one window and now routes each request automatically.

Claude Docs lets users draft documents in a conversation, comment on finished sections, then export to Google Docs or Microsoft Word.

Claude Slides builds and edits presentations inside the same window, with downloads as PowerPoint or PDF files.

Pro and Max plans receive the update first on web, desktop and mobile over the coming weeks. Free and Team tiers follow later.

Claude Design, launched April 17, 2026, now runs inside any conversation, with no separate entry point.

Claude now decides which tool a request needs

Anthropic said customers often struggled to choose the right tab for the right task, which is the problem the merged front end is built to remove. A user who asks for a deck no longer opens a separate surface for it. Claude reads the request and starts the work in place.

The company described the mechanism plainly. “Claude can now figure out what a task needs, so what Cowork and Design can do is available from any conversation,” Anthropic said, with a conversation’s existing context and connected tools carried into the work.

That routing rests on a change shipped three weeks earlier. On August 25 Anthropic merged the memory layer behind chat and Cowork so that context learned in one surface survives into the other, on by default across the Free, Pro and Max plans. Without shared memory, a request routed from a chat into an agentic task would arrive with none of the detail the user had already supplied.

Claude Cowork and chat are merging into one Claude.Ask a quick question or hand over a report, and Claude takes it from there, even after you close your laptop. If something's unclear, Claude asks—you keep the final say.Rolling out to Pro and Max over the next few weeks. pic.twitter.com/87HC2lUjxG— Claude (@claudeai) September 16, 2026

Docs and Slides aim Claude output at Office and Workspace files

Claude Docs starts every document private, then lets the author share it with collaborators by link and take comments on completed parts. Users can open a document on desktop, walk away, and watch the task progress from the mobile app. Exports go to Google Docs and Microsoft Word.

Claude Slides covers creating, editing and presenting a deck from inside the conversation, and downloads it as a PowerPoint or PDF file. Anthropic already offered that export path through Claude Design, which exports to Canva, PDF, PPTX and HTML for subscribers on the Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans. What changed is placement. Design no longer needs its own destination.

Claude Cowork itself stays in beta on web and mobile while running fully on desktop, and it is already included on those same four plans. Anthropic has not said whether the merged front end changes that beta label. SQ Magazine has tracked the product’s growth in its Claude AI usage statistics.

What the announcement does not settle?

Anthropic’s newsroom and the Claude app release notes carried no entry for the merge on launch day, so the published detail comes from briefings given to reporters at TechCrunch and Engadget. That establishes what the company says the feature does. It does not establish how well the routing works, because no accuracy figure, error rate or override control has been disclosed.

Four gaps sit open:

Can a user force a request into chat, Cowork or Design when Claude routes it somewhere else?

What date do the Free and Team tiers get the unified interface?

Do existing Artifacts and Cowork project workspaces migrate, or do they sit alongside the new surface?

Does Cowork leave beta on web and mobile as part of this rollout?

Users already pointing Cowork at local folders should check two settings now that agentic work can begin from any conversation: which folders stay connected, and the toggle that controls whether sensitive topics enter memory. Reviewing both helps reduce the risk of Claude acting on files in a thread the user treated as ordinary chat.

Don’t chase tech news. We track it for you.

One weekly briefing with the launches, AI developments, and breaches that matter. No filler.

Email address

The Bottom Line

The merge trades a navigation decision for a routing decision, and that is a real bet on classifier quality. Every wrong route now costs a user the time it takes to notice Claude went agentic on a question that wanted a two-line answer, or stayed conversational on a task that wanted file access. Anthropic is confident enough in the shared memory layer and the task classifier to make that trade the default for its highest-paying consumer tiers, which is a stronger signal about internal evaluation results than any of the feature copy.

The document and slide exports matter more than the merged navigation. Sending Claude output straight into Word, Google Docs, PowerPoint and PDF puts the assistant inside the file formats that corporate work actually moves in, which is the ground Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini already hold through the suites themselves. Watch for three things over the coming weeks: whether Team and Enterprise customers get the merged interface before the Free tier, whether Anthropic publishes any data on routing quality, and whether Cowork’s beta label comes off. The company’s enterprise AI expansion suggests the business tiers are the ones worth watching.

sourceTexts.title: Anthropic folds Cowork into Claude and launches Docs and Slides
sourceTexts.text:
Anthropic is combining Cowork, its tool for longer tasks, with the main Claude app and introducing two new editors called Claude Docs and Claude Slides.

Now, users do not have to pick between chatting with Claude or assigning it a task. Instead, Claude will decide how to handle each request, according to a company blog post on Wednesday.

Cowork started in January as a separate space for tasks that require more than one response, such as reading a folder of files or putting together a report. VentureBeat reported that Anthropic said users found it confusing to choose where to do their work.

Anthropic’s video introducing the merged Claude chat and Cowork experience. Video: Claude / YouTube

Now, features like breaking tasks into steps, using tools, and working in the background are part of the regular chat. Users can still set limits on how much Claude does before checking in.

Docs and Slides, which are both in beta for paid plans, let Claude create a document or presentation that users and their colleagues can edit directly.

Each project has a single shareable link for both desktop and mobile, and slides can be shown directly in Claude. According to Anthropic, files can be exported to Google formats, PowerPoint, or PDF.

Claude Design, which Anthropic launched in April using Canva’s design engine, will now be part of the main conversation rather than a separate tool. Claude Code, the tool for developers, will remain separate.

Pro and Max subscribers will get these changes first on web, desktop, and mobile in the next few weeks. Team and Free users will get them later. Anthropic said enterprise administrators will have at least 30 days’ notice before the update.

This consolidation has been in progress for some time. Last month, Anthropic combined memory between chat and Cowork, so anything a user shared with one could be used by the other.

OpenAI made a similar move in July by combining ChatGPT and its Codex coding agent into a single desktop app, introducing a new Work mode for knowledge workers. Both companies are targeting office staff who want complete documents and presentations, not just answers in a chat window.

The new editors also put Anthropic in direct competition with established office software. Docs and Slides are similar to Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, and Anthropic has added Claude to Word and made exporting to those formats a key feature.

Anthropic folds Claude Cowork into Claude and adds Docs and Slides

Anthropic is removing the separate Chat-versus-Cowork choice. Claude will decide when a conversation needs longer-running agentic work, while Docs and Slides arrive as beta workspaces.

September 17, 2026

Key points

Claude Code stays separate

Anthropic folds Claude Cowork into Claude, removes the mode switch, adds beta Docs and Slides, and keeps Claude Code separate in a staged rollout.

Anthropic announced on September 16, 2026, that Claude Cowork and Claude Chat are merging into one Claude experience. The practical change is simple: you no longer have to decide whether a task belongs in a quick chat or a separate agentic workspace. Claude is designed to make that call inside the conversation.

The rollout starts with Pro and Max plans across the web, desktop and mobile apps over the following weeks. Team and Free plans are scheduled to follow, while Anthropic says Enterprise administrators will receive at least 30 days’ notice before organizational changes.

The Chat/Cowork choice disappears

The announcement video demonstrates Claude’s unified conversation, the removed Chat/Cowork selector and the output menu for Docs, Slides and Design.

Before the merger, users selected Chat or Cowork before starting work. The new experience removes that upfront decision. A normal conversation can handle a short question, or Claude can shift into longer-running, multi-step work when the request needs tools, connectors, task decomposition or continued execution while the user is away.

Anthropic says Claude asks for permission before taking an action by default. Users can also choose a more autonomous mode in which Claude continues working and checks in when closer review is needed. That keeps the handoff inside one conversation instead of forcing a jump between product surfaces.

The announcement video demonstrates the removed Chat/Cowork selector and the unified output menu for Docs, Slides, Design and Artifacts.

Docs, Slides and Design move into the conversation

The merger is also a packaging change for Claude’s work products. Claude Docs and Claude Slides launch as beta workspaces on paid plans rather than simple files that appear only at the end of a chat.

Claude Docs is an editable, collaborative document workspace. Anthropic says documents can be exported to Microsoft Word or Google Docs. Claude Slides is an editable presentation workspace that can be presented from Claude and exported to PowerPoint or PDF.

Claude Design is now available inside regular conversations while remaining usable as a standalone product. Design, Docs and Slides outputs can be accessed through one shareable link, including on a phone. That gives the unified Claude experience a broader job: not just answering questions, but turning a conversation into a document, presentation or visual project.

Claude Code stays separate

The consolidation does not absorb Claude Code. It remains a separate coding-focused product for work in terminals and integrated development environments against codebases.

That leaves a clear boundary in Anthropic’s product lineup: Claude handles ordinary conversations, agentic tasks and the new document, presentation and design workspaces, while Claude Code remains the dedicated environment for software development.

The company introduced Claude Cowork as a research preview on January 12, 2026, initially as a Claude Max feature in the macOS desktop app for nontechnical work. Its September consolidation folds that separate workspace into the broader Claude experience rather than removing the longer-running capabilities themselves.

sourceTexts.title: Claude Docs and Slides: Anthropic’s beta launch
sourceTexts.text:
Anthropic announced beta tools for creating documents and presentations in Claude conversations. Docs supports collaboration and several export formats; Slides can be presented in Claude or downloaded.

September 25, 2026

Key points

01

Anthropic announced Claude Docs and Claude Slides as beta features on paid plans on September 16, 2026.

02

Anthropic’s Docs Help Center lists Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise for the Docs beta; Enterprise access is off by default until an organization owner enables it.

03

Claude Docs exports to Word, PDF, Markdown and Google Docs; Claude Slides can be presented in Claude or downloaded as PowerPoint or PDF.

04

Docs supports viewer and editor roles, but has no version history or comment-only access.

In this article

01

What Claude Docs and Claude Slides do

02

How Docs, Slides and Design fit into Claude conversations

03

Claude Docs access, sharing and limits

Anthropic announced Claude Docs and Slides as paid-plan beta tools, with editable documents, presentations, collaboration, and practical export options.

On September 16, 2026, Anthropic announced Claude Docs and Claude Slides as beta features on paid Claude plans, bringing document and presentation creation into Claude conversations. Anthropic also announced a staged plan to bring Cowork and ordinary Claude chat into one Claude experience.

What Claude Docs and Claude Slides do

Claude Docs creates rich-text documents that users can edit and share. Claude Slides creates presentations that users can edit, present in Claude and download as PowerPoint or PDF. The two tools serve different jobs, with separate output options:

ProductBeta accessMain useExport or presentation optionsClaude DocsPro, Max, Team and Enterprise are listed for the beta; Enterprise access is off by defaultCreate and edit rich-text documents; collaborate with other editorsWord (.docx), PDF, Markdown (.md) and Google DocsClaude SlidesAnnounced as a beta feature on paid Claude plansCreate and edit presentationsPresent in Claude or download as PowerPoint or PDF

To start a Doc, you can ask in a conversation or choose a template from the Artifacts tab. Claude asks clarifying questions before drafting. You can edit the document yourself, ask Claude to revise it, or use comments and mention @Claude to request changes.

Docs also supports simultaneous editing: people with edit access can work in the same document, with changes appearing in real time. Viewers can read; editors can read, edit, comment and export. A shared document requires a Claude account to open.

For Google’s document tools, Claude Docs lists Google Docs as an export destination. Claude Slides’ listed outputs are PowerPoint and PDF.

How Docs, Slides and Design fit into Claude conversations

Anthropic’s launch video depicts Docs, Slides and Design options in one conversation, then a presentation and a one-page document taking shape.

Anthropic’s announcement also described Claude Design as available from conversations, while standalone use continues. The company’s plan for the unified Claude experience was to make Cowork capabilities available alongside ordinary chat, rather than requiring users to choose a separate mode before starting a task.

Anthropic said the combined experience would begin rolling out to Pro and Max over the weeks following its September 16 announcement, with Team and Free to follow.

Claude Docs access, sharing and limits

Anthropic’s Docs Help Center lists Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise as eligible for the beta. On Enterprise, Docs is off by default until an organization owner enables it.

Sharing depends on the plan. Pro and Max users can share with anyone who has the link. Team and Enterprise users can share with invited people or groups, or across their organization; external sharing is not available on those plans.

Docs has no version history or comment-only access. Charts and diagrams made with connected-app data do not refresh automatically. On iOS and Android, users can request and view Docs, but cannot start from a template, edit a Doc or change its sharing settings.

Docs usage counts toward Claude plan limits, and larger requests use more of those limits. Organizations using customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), zero data retention (ZDR) or a HIPAA-ready configuration cannot use Docs. Anthropic says document-level events appear in the Compliance API activity feed, while edits and comments inside Docs are not recorded there.
